name: Hetzner
summary: A German host that rents cloud VMs by the hour and whole dedicated servers by the month from its own data center parks in Germany and Finland, plus cloud-only sites in the US and Singapore.
intro: Hetzner sells two kinds of machine. Hetzner Cloud servers are VMs on shared or dedicated vCPUs, with Arm (Ampere) types as well as x86, created in seconds through a REST API, the `hcloud` CLI, Terraform or the console. Around them sit the usual cloud parts: Volumes (block storage from 10 GB to 10 TB, each block stored on three physical servers), private Networks, stateful Firewalls at no extra cost, Load Balancers, Primary IPs and an S3-compatible Object Storage built on Ceph. Dedicated root servers are physical machines (AMD-based AX, Intel-based EX, storage-heavy SX, GPU and Dell DX lines) rented by the month, and a Server Auction resells refurbished ones.

Hetzner owns and runs its data center parks in Falkenstein and Nuremberg in Germany and in Tuusula near Helsinki in Finland, all in the `eu-central` network zone. Ashburn (Virginia), Hillsboro (Oregon) and Singapore are cloud-only: they offer the AMD shared and dedicated vCPU types and cloud features, but no dedicated servers, no Arm types and no Object Storage.

Cloud servers have an hourly rate and a monthly cap; you pay whichever is lower, and a partial hour counts as a full one. A server is billed until it is deleted, even when it is switched off, because its resources stay reserved. In the EU the CX, CPX and CAX types include 20 TB of outgoing traffic a month, and only outgoing traffic is billed; in the US and Singapore the allowance is far smaller, from 0.5 to 8 TB depending on type and site. Public IPv4 is extra (€0.50 a month), IPv6 is free.
strengths: Low prices for raw compute and traffic: 20 TB of egress included per EU cloud server, and dedicated servers on the default 1 Gbit uplink have unlimited traffic
One provider for both hourly VMs and monthly bare metal, so a cluster can mix cloud nodes with large dedicated machines
Owned data centers in Germany and Finland under a German company, which suits teams that want EU hosting; the sites are ISO 27001 certified
A plain REST API and CLI, with integrations for Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes, Python and Go listed on the cloud page
limits: The catalog stops at the infrastructure layer: servers, volumes, networks, firewalls, load balancers and object storage, so databases and other services are yours to run
The US and Singapore sites are cloud-only, with a much smaller traffic allowance, and no Arm types or Object Storage

Prices rose sharply in 2026: on 1 April for new and existing products because of RAM and SSD costs, and again on 15 June, when a CCX13 went from €15.99 to €42.99 a month and a CX23 from €3.99 to €5.49
Switching a cloud server off doesn’t stop the bill, and a Volume attaches to one server at a time

snippet.title: Create a cloud server in Falkenstein with the `hcloud` CLI and attach a volume

hcloud server create --name web-1 --type cx23 --image ubuntu-24.04 \
# 100 GB of block storage, formatted and mounted on the server

story: Martin Hetzner, an electrical engineer, founded the company in Gunzenhausen in Bavaria in 1997, with the aim of making internet technology affordable and accessible to more people. It rented its first data center in the middle of Nuremberg in 2001. Rented space limited what it could control, so in 2008 it began building its own data center park in Falkenstein, designed from the ground up and opened in 2009, and it started developing its own servers to depend less on existing products.

In 2015 Hetzner began planning a second park in Tuusula, about 20 km from Helsinki, for the cold climate that lets outside air cool the servers and for the cheap electricity; the C-Lion1 submarine cable between Rostock and Helsinki went live in 2016. In 2018 it launched Hetzner Cloud, because many customer projects needed more flexibility than monthly dedicated servers: for the first time, customers could start servers within seconds.

It then went abroad with cloud-only sites: Ashburn, Virginia in 2021, Hillsboro, Oregon in 2022 for lower latency on the US West Coast, and Singapore in 2024. In 2026 rising memory and SSD prices led to several price rounds, including increases on existing products from 1 April and a steeper repricing of cloud servers from 15 June.

choices.choice: Own data center parks instead of rented space
choices.why: Rented data centers left Hetzner little control over power, cooling and cost; the company says long-term good prices and stable performance need control of its own infrastructure.
The cold climate lets servers be cooled with outside air, electricity is cheap, and the C-Lion1 cable gives a fast link to central Europe.

choices.choice: A cloud next to dedicated servers
choices.why: Customers needed machines they could start and remove quickly, not only servers rented by the month; the cloud added that without leaving Hetzner’s own hardware.

choices.choice: Hourly billing with a monthly cap
choices.why: A short test pays only for the hours used, while a server that runs all month never costs more than its monthly price.
